Top 10 Popular
Attractions inPrachuap Khiri Khan
intro: Prachuap Khiri Khan has it all — the beloved Hua Hin beach, a major temple that draws endless merit-makers, and mountains and caves that photograph beautifully enough to demand a visit. We've picked the 10 attractions people visit most, from the shoreline to the summit, all easy to reach and enjoyable for both families and couples.

blocks.html:
When people think of a beach destination close to Bangkok — somewhere you can do as a day trip or an overnight — Prachuap Khiri Khan is one of the first names that comes up. Hua Hin has a long white-sand beach for horseback rides and seaside relaxation. Over at Khao Takiab, Cicada Market has become the go-to evening meeting point for craft lovers and live-music fans. Drop down into Prachuap city itself and Khao Chong Krachok offers a climb to a panoramic three-bay view. For nature enthusiasts, Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park and Phraya Nakhon Cave are only a short drive further. One province, many different atmospheres in a single trip.

This list covers the places people genuinely talk about most. Wat Huay Mongkol is home to the world's largest Luang Pu Thuat statue; visitors flock daily to pray and crawl beneath the three-headed Erawan elephant. Phraya Nakhon Cave inside Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park holds the Kuha Kharuehat Pavilion — a golden four-sided royal pavilion built in the reign of King Rama V — and the shaft of sunlight that falls onto it at mid-morning is an image people travel here specifically to capture. Vana Nava Water Jungle is Asia's first tropical-forest-themed water park. Rajabhakti Park features bronze statues of seven Thai kings on a sweeping open plaza. Set your itinerary and head out.

blocks.name: Hua Hin Beach
blocks.signature: About 5 kilometres of white sand beach — seaside relaxation, horseback riding and photography along the shoreline
blocks.descHtml:
When you think of Hua Hin, the beach is the first thing that comes to mind. Stretching about 5 kilometres from the town centre to Khao Takiab, the white sand is wide enough for a long walk at any pace. It works for every kind of visitor: families with small children who want shallow water, couples looking for a quiet spot to catch the breeze, and photographers who come to frame the coastline. The signature activity everyone has to try at least once is horseback riding along the shoreline — horses plodding at the water's edge has been a symbol of Hua Hin for so long it's practically part of the town's identity.

The not-to-miss moment is an early morning visit for the sunrise. The water is calm, the sky shifts colour gradually, and multiple reviews rate it among the best sunrise spots in the area. An evening visit brings a cool breeze, lively foot traffic, and the kind of atmosphere that makes it easy to linger. Beyond the horses, popular activities include banana boats, kite flying, paddling in the shallows, and renting a beach chair to sit and watch the sea.

The beach itself is free. Horseback riding is roughly 20 minutes for THB 400, 30 minutes for THB 500, and one hour for THB 1,000. A quick photo on horseback costs about THB 50 per person. Riding services run approximately 06:30–18:00 subject to weather and tides. The beach is open 24 hours and is right in the middle of town — step out from any beachside hotel or restaurant and you're there.

It's popular because it's easy to reach, close to Bangkok, and gives you multiple activities in one place. Google rates it around 4.2 from thousands of reviews. One thing to be aware of: at high tide the beach narrows significantly in some sections — check low-tide times before you go. Vendors and horse handlers along the beach can be persistent; a polite decline is enough. Morning or late afternoon is the most comfortable time to visit.

Evening walk and sea breeze
Watch the sunrise at dawn
Collect shells and paddle in the shallows

blocks.name: Cicada Market
blocks.area: Khao Takiab, Hua Hin, Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.signature: Handmade craft and art market with live music, street food, and seating beneath large trees
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Hua Hin over a weekend and want a night market that goes beyond just eating and shopping, Cicada Market in the Khao Takiab area is worth the visit. From the start it positioned itself as a craft, handmade goods, and art market — so what's on sale here is genuinely different from the average market stall. Expect handmade clothing, jewellery, home decor, whimsical gifts, and artwork from actual working artists. Walking through feels like an open-air gallery shaded by large trees. Great for design lovers, families, couples, and friend groups who want to sit, eat, and relax more than they want to power-shop.

The highlight not to miss is the open-air live music stage at Sasi Open Air Theatre — artists take turns performing throughout the evening, creating a soundtrack that makes the whole outdoor space feel easy and unhurried. There's also an evening variety show with street performers. The street food zone is well-stocked: moo satay, Pad Thai, made-to-order dishes, Western options, fruit juices, beers, and cocktails. Multiple reviews note that the food choices are diverse and don't repeat themselves much — find a spot under the trees, order a plate, and listen to the music in comfort. The decor throughout is thoughtful, with fairy lights and street art that photograph well.

Located near Khao Takiab close to the beach, open Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays from around 16:00–23:00. Free entry with no gate fee. Budget a few hundred THB to eat well and pick up something appealing. The market has been popular for years — Google rates it around 4.3 from over 18,000 reviews — reflecting a strong mix of Thai and international visitors who appreciate how it blends art, music, and food in a single setting.

A few things to know: the market is Fri–Sun only, so a weekday visit finds it closed. Saturday evening is the most crowded; arriving in the early evening gives you a better spot before the peak. Check the day's music schedule on the market's page before you go so you don't miss an artist you'd enjoy.

Handmade crafts and art zone

Sit beneath the large trees and listen to music

blocks.name: Wat Huay Mongkol (Giant Luang Pu Thuat)
blocks.signature: The world's largest Luang Pu Thuat statue — standing prominently in the centre of the temple grounds; crawl beneath the three-headed Erawan elephant and pay respects to Thao Wessuwan and Ai Khai
blocks.descHtml:
Wat Huay Mongkol is the sacred-site destination almost everyone visits when they come to Hua Hin. The defining feature is the giant Luang Pu Thuat statue — claimed to be the largest in the world — cast in metal with a lap width of about 9.9 metres and a height of about 11.5 metres, standing on a three-tiered base in the centre of a broad open plaza. The temple was originally called Wat Huay Kot before receiving its current name. It suits those who want easy, comfortable merit-making — the grounds are flat, the paths are wide, and there are no steep stairs, making it accessible for elderly visitors and families stopping on the way to the beach.

The must-do here is climbing up to pay respects and make offerings at the main statue, then walking over to crawl beneath the three-headed Erawan elephant that flanks the grounds. Visitors traditionally walk under the elephant's belly and toss coins to make a wish for good fortune. Nearby are Ai Khai for business blessings, Thao Wessuwan for wealth and protection, and a monument to King Taksin the Great at the front. Multiple reviews note that a single visit lets you pay respects to many figures at once — good value for the journey.

The overall atmosphere is shaded and pleasant — trees, a pond, and walkways give it more of a park feel than a typical temple. There are fish-feeding points, souvenir and offering shops, food stalls, drinks, and a small café for a rest. Free car park, no admission fee — just optional merit-making donations. Located in Thap Tai sub-district, about 14–15 kilometres from Hua Hin town, roughly 20 minutes by car. Open daily approximately 06:00–20:30.

Its popularity is reflected in a Google rating of 4.6 from tens of thousands of reviews. During festivals — especially the annual Luang Pu Thuat robe-wrapping ceremony — it gets very busy. The open plaza gets strong midday sun; come in the morning or late afternoon, wear a hat or carry an umbrella, and dress modestly as befits a sacred space.
mustOrder: Pay respects and make offerings at the giant Luang Pu Thuat statue
Crawl beneath the three-headed Erawan elephant
Pay respects to Thao Wessuwan and Ai Khai
Feed the fish and walk around the pond

blocks.bestFor: Sacred-site seekers; family groups including elderly visitors

blocks.name: Khao Chong Krachok
blocks.signature: 396 steps to the summit, panoramic three-bay views across 360 degrees, and a troop of monkeys lining the path up
blocks.descHtml:
Khao Chong Krachok is the landmark hill synonymous with Prachuap Khiri Khan city. Anyone who arrives in the three-bay town stops here. It's a modest hill inside the grounds of Wat Thammikaram Worawihan, right along the bay — easy enough to complete in half a day. Perfect for merit-makers, view-seekers, and families who want to get the children moving. The highlight is the 396 concrete steps leading to the summit, where a 360-degree view takes in Ao Noi, Ao Prachuap, and Ao Manao spread out side by side to the horizon, along with a chedi and a replica Buddha footprint to pay respects to.

The experience everyone talks about is shooting photos from the high point in the morning or evening — clear sky, cool sea breeze, the city and coastline spread below in a way that makes you feel like you have the whole vista to yourself. The other thing that's become a signature here is the resident troop of monkeys lining both sides of the path. Reviews consistently warn to hide food and plastic bags, and to keep valuables like sunglasses and phones tucked away because the monkeys are bold and quick. Many people carry a small stick to keep them back.

No entry fee — climbing is free, no charge. Open during daylight hours every day. The location is easy: right next to the city centre along Ao Prachuap, with parking available at the temple below. Anyone who finds the midday heat too much should come early — both for comfort and because the monkeys are calmer in the morning.

Its popularity is backed by a Google rating of 4.6. One practical note: the steps are fairly steep — wear trainers, carry water, and save some energy for the descent. The views make the climb worth every step.
mustOrder: Climb all 396 steps to the summit
360-degree view of the three bays
Pay respects at the chedi and replica Buddha footprint
Shoot photos from the top in the morning or evening

blocks.name: Hua Hin Night Market
blocks.signature: Evening walking street — fresh seafood on ice, desserts, souvenirs, open every night
blocks.descHtml:
Hua Hin Night Market is the evening walking street that has been part of this town for decades. It runs along Dechanuchit Road in the centre of Hua Hin, a short walk from Hua Hin Railway Station. The saying around here is that if you come to Hua Hin and haven't walked this market at night, you haven't really arrived. It works for everyone — families, couples, friend groups, solo travellers — because the roughly 300-metre stretch is packed with food, desserts, and souvenirs from end to end. As the sun goes down the lights come on and the energy picks up steadily through the early evening.

The most talked-about draw is the fresh seafood laid out on ice in long rows to choose from. Duang Jai Seafood and Rot Fai Seafood are names that come up frequently in visitor searches. The smell of grilled prawns, shellfish, crabs, and squid drifts down the whole lane. For those with a sweet tooth, the famous 72 Crêpe stall should not be missed, alongside mango sticky rice and freshly made hot roti. Standard Thai staples are also covered: Pad Thai, oyster omelette, moo satay, and papaya salad — easy to graze through on a long stroll. Beyond food there are clothes, bags, handmade items, lanterns, and souvenirs to browse.

Budget-friendly: no entry fee, most food stalls start at THB 20–60 per item, rising for seafood priced by weight — always ask the price before ordering. Park near Wat Hua Hin or along nearby streets; those arriving by train can walk straight in. Open every night from around 17:00 until late. The best energy is after 19:00 when crowds build.

The market is popular because it delivers everything visitors want in one place: full stomach, souvenirs, and the breezy atmosphere of a seaside resort town after dark. Google gives it around 4.2 from over 20,000 reviews. High season and holiday weekends bring thick crowds that slow the walk; weekdays and off-peak periods are more comfortable. Friday and Saturday evenings are the liveliest; weekday evenings for a more relaxed stroll.
mustOrder: Grilled fresh seafood (Duang Jai Seafood / Rot Fai Seafood)
72 Crêpe
Mango sticky rice and fresh roti
Moo satay, oyster omelette, Pad Thai

blocks.name: Khao Takiab
blocks.signature: A large Buddha image facing the sea, Hua Hin city viewpoint, Wat Khao Takiab and Wat Khao Krailas — plus a resident troop of monkeys
blocks.descHtml:
Khao Takiab is the small hill that juts into the sea at the southern end of Hua Hin Beach. It combines everything a Hua Hin visitor typically wants in one place — a temple, a large Buddha image, a sea viewpoint, and a troop of monkeys who claim the hill as their own. Ideal for those who want temple merit-making with a great view at the same time, regardless of whether you're a family, a couple, or a foreign visitor wanting to see Hua Hin from above. It's known well enough that many people call it Monkey Mountain.

The must-see is the large Pang Ham Samut Buddha image — around 16 metres tall — standing facing the sea at the foot of the hill. Climb the stairs to Wat Khao Takiab above, where a chedi, a Guanyin statue, and a viewpoint look out over Hua Hin Beach and the town in both directions. Reviews consistently say the view here is genuinely good, especially in the morning and late afternoon when the light is soft. The monkeys are visible all the way up — charming but mischievous.

Free entry. If you'd like to make merit, sets of offerings are available to donate. Open every day approximately 08:00–18:00. Located at the southern end of Hua Hin Beach in the Nong Kae area, a short drive or songthaew ride from town. About 150 steps to the temple; those unable to walk up can arrange a vehicle to the top. Google rates it around 4.1 from thousands of reviews — most visitors come away pleased with the views and the atmosphere.

One important note about the monkeys: never carry food, snacks, or plastic bags in your hands — the monkeys are fast and used to people. Shiny things like glasses and phones need to be secured. Motorbike riders should park carefully. Dress modestly as it is a temple, and coming in the late afternoon gives you both good sunset light and thinner crowds.

blocks.name: Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park (Phraya Nakhon Cave)
blocks.area: Sam Roi Yot District, Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.signature: Phraya Nakhon Cave with the Kuha Kharuehat Pavilion — a beam of sunlight falling onto the royal pavilion is the defining image of the site
blocks.descHtml:
Phraya Nakhon Cave is a large limestone cave inside Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park that virtually no one who comes to Prachuap Khiri Khan is willing to skip. The defining image is the Kuha Kharuehat Pavilion — a golden four-sided royal pavilion built in the reign of King Rama V — standing in the main chamber of the cave. When a shaft of sunlight drops through the cave ceiling and falls exactly onto the pavilion, the scene is one many visitors describe as a must-see once in a lifetime. It suits nature enthusiasts, photographers, and those willing to trade a moderate climb for a view that rewards the effort.

The unmissable moment is the light beam hitting the pavilion, best around 10:30–11:30. The effect is clearest from cool-season through early hot-season (roughly November to May). Beyond the pavilion, the chamber holds curtain-like stalactites and stalagmites, and unusually tall trees that have grown inside the cave where the light enters. Getting there requires either a boat from Ban Bang Pu or a hike over Khao Thian, followed by a section of stone steps up to the cave. To be straight with you: the ascent is steep in parts — most reviews recommend pacing yourself and leaving enough time.

National park entry fees: Thai adults THB 40, children THB 20; foreign adults THB 200, children THB 100. Boat hire from Ban Bang Pu is around THB 400 per vessel, carrying multiple passengers, with a sea view included on the ten-minute ride. The park opens daily approximately 08:00–16:30. Going early in the morning maximises the chance of catching good light and avoids the hottest part of the descent.

This is consistently ranked the most visited spot in Sam Roi Yot District, combining history, nature, and photography in one place. Before you go: wear trainers or trekking shoes with good grip as the rocks are sharp and slippery; bring your own water as there are no shops along the trail; and watch for long-tailed macaques who may try to snatch food or valuables. Keep bags closed and enjoy the hike.

blocks.name: Vana Nava Water Jungle Hua Hin
blocks.signature: Asia's first tropical-forest-themed water park, with thrilling slides including Abyss and a children's play zone
blocks.descHtml:
Vana Nava Water Jungle is Asia's first tropical-forest-themed water park, set in the middle of Hua Hin on 20 rai of land transformed to resemble a real rainforest — over 200,000 trees and plants mean the grounds feel lush and shaded, nothing like the open, sun-baked layouts of typical water parks. This suits families with young children, couples, friend groups who enjoy intense rides, and international visitors looking for a full-day cool-off activity. One ticket covers over 20 rides.

The ride most people talk about is Abyss — a giant funnel slide that generates intense centrifugal force. Essential for thrill-seekers. Next is AquaLoop, a near-vertical drop into a looping tube, and Boomerango, a long multi-rider slide that stays fun across multiple runs. The Vana Nava Falls artificial waterfall at around 31 metres is a great photo point. Families with small children have a dedicated children's zone and a wave pool so the little ones can enjoy themselves without tackling the big rides. Real reviews frequently praise the number of lifeguards, strong safety practices, friendly staff, and shorter queues on weekdays.

Walk-up tickets are around THB 990 per adult; booking online in advance or through a promotion is noticeably cheaper. A minority of reviews flag the ticket price as high and note the buffet is average; most feel a full day of entertainment justifies the cost. Book in advance and arrive early to get more rides in before the crowds build.

Located in Nong Kae sub-district on Phetkasem Road, convenient from Hua Hin town, next to Holiday Inn group hotels. Normal hours 11:00–17:00 daily, sometimes extended during holidays and high season. Google rates it 4.4 from thousands of reviews. Bring your own swimwear, apply waterproof sunscreen, and clear your schedule for the whole day — there's enough here to fill it.
mustOrder: Abyss — the giant funnel slide
AquaLoop — vertical drop into a loop
Boomerango — long multi-rider slide
Vana Nava Falls artificial waterfall

blocks.name: Rajabhakti Park
blocks.area: Hua Hin District (Royal Thai Army area), Prachuap Khiri Khan
blocks.signature: Bronze statues of seven Thai kings, averaging around 13.9 metres tall — a sweeping outdoor plaza with mountain backdrop
blocks.descHtml:
Rajabhakti Park is a large commemorative plaza on Royal Thai Army land in Hua Hin. The centrepiece is seven bronze royal statues — from King Ramkhamhaeng the Great through to King Rama V — each averaging around 13.9 metres, arranged on a sweeping open plaza with a mountain backdrop. It suits history lovers, families bringing elderly relatives to pay their respects, and photographers looking for a grand setting without an entry fee.

The must-do is walking up to stand beneath the statues and look up at their scale — reviews consistently describe them as impressively large and dignified. The bronze casting detail is remarkable. The park also provides a free tram service around the plaza with a guide who narrates the history of each king on board, giving you both the experience and the knowledge at the same time. The front-facing angle that captures all seven statues in a single frame is the go-to photo position.

Free entry, with donation boxes for those who wish to contribute. Open daily 08:00–18:00. Located about 8 kilometres south of Hua Hin town along Phetkasem Road — easy by car or hired transport, with a large car park. The grounds are kept clean, orderly, and calm with the atmosphere of a public institution.

Things to know: as an area under Thai Army administration, modest dress is expected and may be required — covering to the ankles in some periods. The plaza is almost entirely exposed to the sun with little shade, and the surfaces and statues reflect heat significantly. Morning or late afternoon is strongly recommended — bring a hat or umbrella. This spot is popular for combining the sacred, the beautiful, and the free.

Free tram ride with guide narration around the plaza
Front-facing angle to photograph all seven statues together

blocks.name: Seenspace Huahin
blocks.signature: Hua Hin's first beachfront community mall — bare-concrete minimalist architecture, every building with a sea view
blocks.priceRange: Free to enter · drinks from THB 190
blocks.descHtml:
Seenspace Huahin is Hua Hin's first beachfront community mall, tucked away at the end of Soi Hua Hin 35. The selling point is a cluster of bare-concrete loft buildings designed by a well-known architecture team — minimalist, raw, and staggered so that every building faces the Gulf of Thailand. Walking in feels like entering a separate world. The concept is Eat, Lay, Play, Relax. It suits café lovers, photographers, couples, and friend groups who want to sit, breathe sea air, and take their time, rather than power through a shopping run.

The most talked-about spot is Oasis x Seenspace — a day-club pool bar with an infinity pool, roughly 24 sun loungers around it, and a setting that lets you sip drinks and watch the sunset over the sea. Another popular corner is Sundance Lounge, a glass-walled café where you can sample teas before ordering. The bare-concrete-against-sea backdrop is a favourite photo subject. There's also a small hotel tucked into the complex. The overall feel is airy, relaxed, and best in the mid-afternoon through to sunset.

Free to enter. The Oasis pool bar zone in the evening typically has a minimum food spend per person; drinks start at around THB 190, with meals running higher than a typical local restaurant. Located along the beach south of the town centre — easy by car. Open Mon–Fri 12:00–21:00, Sat–Sun and holidays 11:00–22:00 (individual outlets may vary slightly).

Its appeal is that it's a beachside mall unlike any other — close to Bangkok, possible as a day trip, with no equivalent elsewhere. One thing to know: several of the fashion retail outlets have gradually closed, leaving the complex driven mainly by cafés, restaurants, and the Oasis zone. If you come expecting extensive retail, you may be surprised by how quiet the shopping is. But for atmosphere, sea views, sitting, and shooting photos — it still delivers well. Best visited from mid-afternoon into sunset.

blocks.title: Know before you go — Prachuap Khiri Khan

items.title: Getting around
items.text: Attractions are spread across several zones — driving or renting a car is the most convenient option. Within Hua Hin, Grab and motorbike taxis work well. Phraya Nakhon Cave requires a boat or a hike over the mountain.

items.title: Carry cash
items.text: Cicada Market, Hua Hin Night Market, street-food stalls, boat fares, and national park entry fees mostly require cash. Keep small notes and coins handy.

items.title: Avoid queues and peak crowds
items.text: Cicada Market is open Fri–Sun only and gets crowded in the evening. Phraya Nakhon Cave is best visited early morning to catch the good light and quieter conditions. Pre-booking Vana Nava tickets online skips the ticket queue.

items.title: Watch out for monkeys
items.text: Khao Chong Krachok and Khao Takiab both have resident monkey troops along the path up. Never hold food or plastic bags visibly, and secure glasses and valuables in your bag.

items.title: Dress for temples
items.text: Wat Huay Mongkol, Khao Takiab, and other sacred sites require modest dress — shoulders and knees covered. Remove shoes at designated points and make offerings at your own discretion.

items.title: Language and menus
items.text: Major Hua Hin attractions have reasonable English signage and menus, and most hospitality staff speak basic English. At street markets and smaller stalls, a translation app or pointing at pictures works well.

blocks.title: Plan an efficient Prachuap Khiri Khan day trip
blocks.html:
Group attractions by zone to save time. The Hua Hin zone clusters Hua Hin Beach, Cicada Market, Khao Takiab, Vana Nava, Rajabhakti Park, and Seenspace Huahin close together — cover them through the day and finish with dinner at Hua Hin Night Market.

If Phraya Nakhon Cave inside Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park is on the itinerary, set aside a full day and leave early — you'll need time for the boat or mountain hike plus the cave climb. The pavilion light hits around mid-morning so the timing works well for an early start. For Khao Chong Krachok in Prachuap city, late afternoon with softer sun makes the 396 steps more manageable, and the three-bay views from the top are especially clear. Watch for the monkeys on the way up.

blocks.text: Covering Prachuap Khiri Khan with an overnight stay is far more relaxing than rushing back in one day. Choose beachfront Hua Hin to walk to the Night Market, or stay near Khao Takiab for a quieter base close to Cicada Market. Compare and book in advance.

faq.q: What are the must-see attractions in Prachuap Khiri Khan?
faq.a: For a first visit, Hua Hin Beach and Khao Chong Krachok are the two essential stops. Hua Hin Beach is a 5-kilometre white-sand shoreline in the town centre; Khao Chong Krachok in Prachuap city has 396 steps leading to a 360-degree three-bay view. For sacred-site seekers add Wat Huay Mongkol and its giant Luang Pu Thuat statue; for nature, Phraya Nakhon Cave in Khao Sam Roi Yot is unmissable.

faq.q: What are the highlights of Prachuap Khiri Khan?
faq.a: There's something for every interest. Sea and sand at Hua Hin Beach and Khao Takiab; walking markets like Cicada Market and Hua Hin Night Market; Phraya Nakhon Cave with the Kuha Kharuehat Pavilion and its famous light beam; Wat Huay Mongkol with the world's largest Luang Pu Thuat; photo landmarks like Rajabhakti Park and Seenspace Huahin; and Vana Nava Water Jungle for those who want rides.

faq.q: How much does it cost to visit attractions in Prachuap Khiri Khan?
faq.a: Many are free: Hua Hin Beach, Khao Chong Krachok, Cicada Market, Hua Hin Night Market, Khao Takiab, Wat Huay Mongkol, and Rajabhakti Park (merit-making at own discretion). Phraya Nakhon Cave inside Khao Sam Roi Yot charges Thai adults THB 40, foreigners THB 200, and boat hire around THB 400 per vessel. Vana Nava Water Jungle walk-up adult tickets are around THB 990; book online for a better rate.

faq.q: How do I get around and where do I park in Prachuap Khiri Khan?
faq.a: A personal car is the most convenient option given how spread out the attractions are. Popular spots like Hua Hin Beach, Cicada Market, Vana Nava, and Rajabhakti Park all have car parks. Within Hua Hin town in the evening, Grab or motorbike taxis are easier to manage. Phraya Nakhon Cave requires a boat from Bang Pu or a mountain hike; parking is at Bang Pu beach.

faq.q: When do attractions in Prachuap Khiri Khan open?
faq.a: Cicada Market is open Fri–Sun only, evenings. Hua Hin Night Market runs every evening. Rajabhakti Park opens approximately 08:00–18:00. Vana Nava runs daytime sessions. Hua Hin Beach, Khao Chong Krachok, and Khao Takiab are accessible all day. For Khao Chong Krachok and Phraya Nakhon Cave, daytime visits are recommended for safety and good light.
